\textbf{Quiz 3}

\vspace{2em}

\textbf{Multiple Choice Questions (Single correct)}\\[0.5em]
\emph{Instructions: Select the correct option with a short explanation.}

\begin{enumerate}[label=Q\arabic*., leftmargin=*]
\item \duallayerbox{In a standard RNN, what is the primary purpose of the ``hidden state''?}{In a standard RNN, which component stores the final output of the sequence?}

\textbf{A.} To store the final output of the entire sequence.\\
\textbf{B.} To act as a memory that carries information from previous time steps\\
\textbf{C.} To calculate the loss function for the current word\\
\textbf{D.} To normalize the input embeddings

\item \duallayerbox{Why is the Softmax function typically used in the final layer of a Neural Language Model?}{In training deep networks, which option best describes a method to prevent exploding gradients?}

\textbf{A.} To ensure the output values sum to 1, representing a probability distribution\\
\textbf{B.} To prevent the gradients from exploding\\
\textbf{C.} To increase the speed of the training process\\
\textbf{D.} To allow the model to handle variable-length sequences

\item \duallayerbox{What is a key limitation of feed-forward neural networks for NLP tasks?}{Which option states that such networks cannot use embeddings in NLP models?}

\textbf{A.} They cannot use embeddings\\
\textbf{B.} They assume fixed input size and struggle with temporal order\\
\textbf{C.} They cannot be trained with gradient descent\\
\textbf{D.} They do not use activation functions

\item \duallayerbox{What is the purpose of the ``Forward Pass'' in training?}{During optimization, which step is responsible for updating the network weights?}

\textbf{A.} To update weights based on the loss\\
\textbf{B.} To calculate the predicted output and compute the loss\\
\textbf{C.} To unroll the network into a sequence\\
\textbf{D.} To calculate the gradient for each parameter

\item \duallayerbox{What is true about the weights $U$, $V$, and $W$ across different timestamps in an RNN?}{In an RNN, which statement says that the weights are randomly reinitialized at each step?}

\textbf{A.} They are randomly re-initialized at every step\\
\textbf{B.} They are reused across timestamps\\
\textbf{C.} They increase in value as the sequence progresses\\
\textbf{D.} Only the output weight $V$ is reused

\item \duallayerbox{Suppose all activation functions in a 3-layer neural network are linear. What is the effective model equivalent to?}{Which option describes a model that can represent non-linear decision boundaries using hierarchical splits?}

\textbf{A.} A deeper network with more representational power\\
\textbf{B.} A single linear model\\
\textbf{C.} A recurrent neural network\\
\textbf{D.} A decision tree

\item \duallayerbox{When training an RNN for language modeling using teacher forcing, the model predicts:}{In free-running inference (without teacher forcing), the model predicts the next word using what history?}

\textbf{A.} The next word given the predicted history\\
\textbf{B.} The next word given the ground-truth history\\
\textbf{C.} The current word given itself\\
\textbf{D.} All words simultaneously

\item \duallayerbox{In an RNN, the hidden state at time $t$ depends on:}{In a feed-forward network without recurrence, a unit’s activation at layer t depends on:}

\textbf{A.} Only the input at time $t$\\
\textbf{B.} Only the hidden state at time $t-1$\\
\textbf{C.} Both the input at time $t$ and the hidden state at time $t-1$\\
\textbf{D.} All future inputs

\item \duallayerbox{Consider a neural network layer defined as: $h = f(Wx)$. The input vector $x$ has shape $(n\_0 \textbackslash{}times 1)$, and the output vector $h$ has shape $(n\_1 \textbackslash{}times 1)$. What must be the shape of $W$?}{If we instead write the operation as $h\^{}T = x\^{}T W$, with $x$ of shape $(1 \textbackslash{}times n\_0)$ and $h$ of shape $(1 \textbackslash{}times n\_1)$, what must be the shape of $W$?}

\textbf{A.} $(n_0 \times n_1)$\\
\textbf{B.} $(n_1 \times n_0)$\\
\textbf{C.} $(n_0 \times 1)$\\
\textbf{D.} $(1 \times n_1)$

\item \duallayerbox{What is the main role of backpropagation in neural network training?}{In a deployed neural network used only for making predictions, what is the primary operation performed?}

\textbf{A.} To compute predictions during inference\\
\textbf{B.} To calculate gradients of the loss with respect to parameters\\
\textbf{C.} To initialize weights randomly\\
\textbf{D.} To normalize input data

\end{enumerate}
